reason: This text fragment (2 Chronicles 18-19) describes military and political events involving King Jehoshaphat and King Ahab, culminating in Ahab's death in battle and Jehoshaphat's return to Jerusalem. While a prophet (Jehu son of Hanani) does rebuke King Jehoshaphat, attributing God's wrath to his alliance with the wicked Ahab, this rebuke is directed at the king's personal actions, not at the Hebrew people collectively. The text does not depict the Hebrew people suffering greatly, nor does it show leaders telling the people that their suffering is their own fault. The passage focuses on leadership decisions and consequences at the royal level, not on mass suffering of the people attributed to their own wrongdoing.
